questions.question: Which Central agency issues currency notes on behalf of Central Government?
questions.questionHtml: Which Central agency issues currency notes on behalf of Central Government?
questions.solution:
Option 3 is correct, i.e. Reserve Bank of India. 

  • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is India's highest monetary institution.
  • RBI was established in 1935 by the RBI Act 1934.
  • RBI- Foreign Reserve, bank of banks, acts as banker and debt controller of the Government of India.
  • It is also responsible for printing notes and managing the supply of money in the Indian economy.
  • The Reserve Bank of India has the monopoly of printing the currency in the country.
  • It has the right to issue all types of notes except one rupee note.

Note-

  • Currency notes and coins of one rupee and lower denominations are issued by the Ministry of Finance.
  • Under the Coinage Act, 1906, the Government of India has the sole right to mint coins.
  • According to Section 24(1) of the RBI Act, 1934, RBI is not entitled to issue banknote of denomination of value of one rupee.
  • The currency note of one rupee is issued by the Ministry of Finance and signed by the Finance Secretary of India.

questions.question: Who decides repo rate, reverse repo rate and bank rate?
questions.questionHtml: Who decides repo rate, reverse repo rate and bank rate?
questions.solution:
Option 2 is correct, i.e. Reserve Bank of India.

Key Points

  • Repo Rate:- It is a rate at which the central bank (RBI) lends money to its clients against the government securities.
  • Reverse Repo- It is the rate at which the central bank (RBI) borrows money from its clients.
  • Reverse Repo is used in India as a tool in which banks will give their surplus fund to RBI for a short-term period and earn money.
  • The repo rate is always higher than the reverse repo rate.
  • Repo and Reverse repo rates are decided by the Monitory policy committee (MPC) of RBI.
  • A bank rate is the interest rate at which a nation's central bank lends money to domestic banks, often in the form of very short-term loans. Managing the bank rate is a method by which central banks affect economic activity.
  • Lower bank rates can help to expand the economy by lowering the cost of funds for borrowers, and higher bank rates help to reign in the economy when inflation is higher than desired.
  • SEBI-
    • SEBI is the Securities and Exchange Board of India.
    • It is the regulator of the Indian securities market and was established in the year 1988.
    •  The headquarters of SEBI located in Mumbai.
    • It was given statutory powers through the SEBI Act, 1992 on 30 January 1992, thus making it a statutory body
  • NABARD  NABARD refers to the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.

Founded

12 July 1982

Headquarter

Mumbai, India

Chairman

Shri Shaji K V

questions.question: What is a government budget?
questions.questionHtml: What is a government budget?

options.text: A report on the economic growth of a country.
options.html: A report on the economic growth of a country.

options.text: A plan for managing personal finances.
options.html: A plan for managing personal finances.

options.text: A financial statement of a government's expected revenue and expenditure for a specific period.
options.html: A financial statement of a government's expected revenue and expenditure for a specific period.

options.text: A document outlining foreign policy goals.
options.html: A document outlining foreign policy goals.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3

Key Points

  • A government budget is a financial statement of a government's expected revenue and expenditure for a specific period, usually a fiscal year.
  • The budget outlines the government's financial plans, including how it intends to allocate resources to various sectors such as defense, education, healthcare, and infrastructure.
  • It serves as a tool for economic policy, allowing the government to manage the economy by controlling public spending and taxation.
  • The budget also includes proposals for new taxes or changes to existing tax rates, as well as plans for borrowing and debt management.
  • It reflects the government's priorities and is a key document for ensuring transparency and accountability in public finance.

Additional Information

  • The government budget is typically presented annually in the parliament or legislative assembly by the finance minister.
  • It is subject to debate and approval by the legislative body before being implemented.
  • The budget process involves several stages, including proposal, review, approval, implementation, and evaluation.
  • Effective budgeting is crucial for maintaining fiscal discipline and achieving sustainable economic growth.
  • Governments around the world use budgets to plan for both short-term and long-term financial goals.

questions.question: GDP is an indicator of a country’s economy. What does ‘D’ in GDP stand for?

questions.solution: GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product, which is the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period. The 'D' in GDP refers to the domestic aspect of the country's economy, meaning that only goods and services produced within the country's borders are included in the calculation.

questions.question: Trade agreement between two parties is called:
questions.questionHtml: Trade agreement between two parties is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is bilateral.
Key Points

  • A bilateral trade agreement is a pact between two parties, countries, or regions that outlines the terms and conditions for trade between them.
    • In it, both parties agree to reduce or eliminate trade barriers such as tariffs and quotas to promote trade and investment.
    • It can help to increase economic growth, create job opportunities, and improve the standard of living in both countries.
    • India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) are examples of bilateral agreements.
  • Trade Agreements are treaties in which a country promises to engage in fewer trade protections with another country (or countries) to engage in more trade.
    • It can be between two countries or between many countries.
    • Important terms of trade between them include tariffs, quotas, restrictions on imports and exports, and provisions such as trade facilitation, intellectual property rights, and investment protection.

Additional Information

  • A multilateral trade agreement involves three or more countries or regions that agree to reduce or eliminate trade barriers.
    • The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), among the 15 members, is an example.
    • The World Trade Organization (WTO) is another example of a multilateral trade agreement.
  • A tripartite trade agreement involves three parties, usually countries or regions, that agree to promote trade and investment between them.
    • The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) is an example of a tripartite trade agreement between the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
  • A unilateral trade agreement is a decision made by one country or region to reduce or eliminate trade barriers without the agreement of another party.
    • This is usually a preferential arrangement that a developed country makes for imports from developing countries.
    • The United States has unilateral trade policies under the Generalized System of Preferences.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Mahatma Gandhi is INCORRECT?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements about Mahatma Gandhi is INCORRECT?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi was born in 1869 in Porbandar.
options.html: Mahatma Gandhi was born in 1869 in Porbandar.

options.text: In 1942, he launched the Quit India Movement
options.html: In 1942, he launched the Quit India Movement

options.text: He led the Champaran Satyagraha in 1910.
options.html: He led the Champaran Satyagraha in 1910.

options.text: He led the Dandi Salt March in 1930.
options.html: He led the Dandi Salt March in 1930.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is He led the Champaran Satyagraha in 1910.

Key Points

  • Mahatma Gandhi was born in 1869 in Porbandar.
  • In 1942, he launched the Quit India Movement.
  • He led the Dandi Salt March in 1930.
  • The Champaran Satyagraha was actually led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1917, not 1910.

Additional Information

  • Mahatma Gandhi is known as the Father of the Nation in India.
  • He employed the principles of non-violence and civil disobedience to lead India to independence from British rule.
  • The Champaran Satyagraha was Gandhi's first active involvement in the Indian freedom struggle, focusing on the plight of indigo farmers in Champaran, Bihar.
  • The Quit India Movement was a major civil disobedience movement launched during World War II, demanding an end to British rule in India.
  • The Dandi Salt March was a pivotal event in the Indian independence movement, where Gandhi led a 240-mile march to produce salt from seawater in defiance of British salt laws.

questions.question: Due to rapid urbanisation, the human lifestyle has changed severely; obesity is a major health issue in such condition. Which of the following is a reason for obesity?
questions.questionHtml: Due to rapid urbanisation, the human lifestyle has changed severely; obesity is a major health issue in such condition. Which of the following is a reason for obesity?

options.text: Excessive intake of high calorie foods
options.html: Excessive intake of high calorie foods

options.text: Lack of vitamins in regular diet
options.html: Lack of vitamins in regular diet

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Excessive intake of high calorie foods

Key Points

  • Excessive intake of high calorie foods is a primary reason for obesity, especially in rapidly urbanizing areas.
  • Urbanization often leads to lifestyle changes that include increased consumption of fast food, sugary beverages, and other high-calorie, low-nutrient foods.
  • This dietary shift, combined with reduced physical activity, contributes significantly to weight gain and obesity.
  • Obesity is associated with various health issues such as diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and hypertension.

Additional Information

  • Obesity is defined as having a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher.
  • Urban environments often provide less opportunity for physical activity due to sedentary jobs and limited access to recreational areas.
  • Public health initiatives aimed at reducing obesity often focus on promoting healthier eating habits and increasing physical activity.
  • Other factors contributing to obesity include genetics, metabolism, behavior, and culture.
  • Addressing obesity requires a multifaceted approach including education, policy changes, and community support.

questions.question: Which of the following sectors was the focus of the first Five-Year Plan?

questions.question: In which type of economy there is neither exports nor imports?
questions.questionHtml: In which type of economy there is neither exports nor imports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Closed.

  • An economy having no economic relationship with other countries is called a closed economy.
    • There is neither exports nor imports in a closed economy.
    • Goods are produced and consumed by the same households within a closed economy.
    • The hunter-gatherer societies are the best examples of a closed economy.
    • A closed economy should be entirely self-sufficient.
    • There are no nations that have economies that are completely closed in reality.
  • An economy that has economic relations with other countries of the world is called an open economy.
    • There should be exports and imports in an open economy.
    • Exporting is the process of selling goods or services to a foreign country.
    • Importing is the process of buying goods or services from a foreign country.
  • The economy that left to the free market, and part of it is managed by the government called a mixed economy.
    • Both privately owned businesses and governments play important roles in a mixed economy.
  • The interconnected worldwide economic activities that take place between multiple countries is called a global economy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a capital good?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a capital good?
questions.solution:
Option 1 is correct, Food and Clothing.

Food and Clothing is part of Non-durables consumer goods.

  • Capital Good-
    • Capital goods are tangible assets that one business produces which in turn gets used by the second business to produce consumer goods. Examples include vehicles, machinery, equipment, buildings, vehicles, tools.
  • Consumer durables-
    • Our daily use items and household items are called consumer durables. From fridge, TV, AC to packaged food, clothes all come in consumer durables. Consumer durables can be divided into two categories based on their usage.
  • Durable consumer goods-
    • There are such items in this category which are used for a long time. Electronic appliances, fridges, ACs, washing machines, fans, cars, mobiles, etc. used in kitchens come in durables consumer goods.
  • Non-durables consumer goods-
    • Items that are finished immediately after use are called non-durables consumer goods.
    • Their age may also be a few years. For example, clothes, food items, cosmetics, medicines, etc. fall into this category.

questions.question: What is a fiscal year?

The correct answer is A year that represents the financial reporting period for the government.

Key Points

questions.question: What organisms are dependent on the producers either directly or indirectly for their sustenance?
questions.questionHtml: What organisms are dependent on the producers either directly or indirectly for their sustenance?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Consumers

Consumers are organisms which consume the products and hence they depend on the producers since producers produce the products.

Key Points

  • We know that the main source of energy is the sun i.e. solar energy. Solar energy is “fixed” by the green plants by the photosynthetic process. Upon receiving the photon, photosynthesis starts.
  • By this carbon dioxide and water react to form glucose and oxygen. This is how plants and some other photosynthetic organisms produce their own food. Hence, they are called producers.
  • All organisms directly or indirectly depend on plants for their food. Plants produce their own food by photosynthesis.
  • Herbivores depend on plants for their food.
  • All carnivores depend on herbivores or other carnivores for their food.
  • Omnivores depend on both plants and animals for their food.

questions.question: National defence, roads, government administration are examples of which types of goods?
questions.questionHtml: National defence, roads, government administration are examples of which types of goods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Public goodsKey Points

  •  Public goods are those that are non-excludable and non-rivalrous.
    • This means that:
      • Non-excludable: Once provided, no one can be excluded from using them.
      • Non-rivalrous: One person’s use of the good does not reduce its availability for others.
  • Public goods like national defence, roads, and government administration are essential services that benefit the entire population

Additional Information

  • Complementary Goods:
    • These are goods that are used together, where the use of one increases the demand for the other (e.g., cars and petrol).
    • Example: Cars and petrol, printers and ink cartridges, or smartphones and apps.
    • A rise in the price of one complementary good (e.g., petrol) may decrease the demand for the other (e.g., cars).
  • Private Goods:
    • Private goods are goods that are both excludable (producers can prevent people who do not pay for them from using them) and rivalrous (one person’s use of the good reduces its availability to others).
    • Example: Food, clothing, and personal gadgets.
    • Excludability: Producers can prevent non-payers from accessing the goods.
    • Rivalry: Consumption by one individual reduces the availability for others
  • ​ Supplementary Goods:
    • These are goods that can be used as alternatives to other goods, meaning their consumption is related to or in place of another (e.g., tea and coffee as substitutes).
    • Alternatives: Consumers may choose one good over the other based on price or preference.
    • Impact on Demand: A price increase in one will generally increase demand for its substitute.
    • Example: Tea and coffee, butter and margarine.

questions.question: In India, Micro Finance Institutions primarily target which segment of the population?
questions.questionHtml: In India, Micro Finance Institutions primarily target which segment of the population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Low-income individuals and small businesses.

Key Points

  • Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) are financial entities that provide small loans to people who do not have access to traditional banking services.
  • In India, MFIs primarily target low-income individuals and small businesses to help them improve their livelihoods.
  • These institutions aim to promote financial inclusion by providing credit to those who are underserved by formal financial institutions.
  • MFIs often provide loans for purposes such as starting or expanding a small business, education, healthcare, and housing.
  • By targeting low-income segments, MFIs help in poverty alleviation and economic development.

Additional Information

Microfinance Term Description
Microcredit Small loans given to individuals or small businesses to meet their financial needs.
Self-Help Groups (SHGs) Groups of 10-20 people, usually women, who pool their savings and lend to members.
Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) Groups of individuals who take loans collectively and are jointly liable for repayment.
Financial Inclusion Ensuring access to financial services for all segments of society, particularly the underserved.
Micro Savings Small savings accounts offered to low-income individuals to encourage saving habits.
Micro Insurance Insurance products designed to be affordable for low-income individuals.

questions.question: A situation where the expenditure of the government exceeds its revenue is known as _____.
questions.questionHtml: A situation where the expenditure of the government exceeds its revenue is known as _____.
questions.solution:
Option 2 is correct, i.e. Deficit Financing.

Key Points

  • A situation where the expenditure of the government exceeds its revenue is known as Deficit Financing. 
  • In the case of Deficit Financing, the government has to either borrow or look for other means to cover the expenditure.
  • As per the National Planning Commission of India, ‘deficit financing’ term is used to denote the direct addition to gross national expenditure through budget deficits.
  • The deficits can be met by raising the rates of taxation. It can also be done by increasing the price of public utility services.
  • There can be many deficits- Budget deficit, Revenue deficit, Fiscal Deficit, Monetized Fiscal Deficit, etc.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a savings account?
questions.questionHtml: What is the purpose of a savings account?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2) Earning interest on deposits

Key Points

  • The primary purpose of a savings account is to allow individuals to deposit money and earn interest on those deposits.
  • Savings accounts provide a secure place to store money while growing the balance through accumulated interest over time.
  • These accounts are typically used for saving money for future needs or emergencies, rather than for day-to-day transactions.
  • Interest rates on savings accounts can vary depending on the financial institution and the type of savings account.
  • Savings accounts often come with certain limitations on the number of withdrawals or transfers that can be made each month.

Additional Information

  • Obtaining a mortgage loan (Option 1) is typically done through a different type of loan account, not a savings account.
  • Making day-to-day transactions (Option 3) is generally done through a checking account or a similar transactional account.
  • Paying bills online (Option 4) is often facilitated by checking accounts or online payment platforms, not directly through savings accounts.

questions.question: How is per capita income calculated?
questions.questionHtml: How is per capita income calculated?
questions.solution: Per capita income, also called income per person is the mean income of the people in a country or an economic unit. It is calculated by dividing the GDP or gross national income by the population.

questions.question: Which of the following Steel plants of India does NOT come under the Public Sector?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Steel plants of India does NOT come under the Public Sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. TISCO

  • The three major plants of Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela are maintained by the 'Steel Authority of India Limited' (SAIL).
  • Steel Plant Details
    TISCO
    • Tata Steel, also known as 'TISCO', is a large steel company in the private sector.
    • It was established in 1907 in Jamshedpur, Jharkhand and its headquarters are located in Mumbai.
    Rourkela Steel Plant
    • Rourkela Steel Plant is the first public sector integrated steel plant in India.
    • The factory was established in 1955 in Orissa in collaboration with Germany.

    • It is a steel plant located in Bhilai, Chhattisgarh, India.

    • It was established in 1959 in Kolkata during the Second Five-Year Plan.

questions.question: The movement of people across regions and territories is called ________.
questions.questionHtml: The movement of people across regions and territories is called ________.
questions.solution: Migration refers to the movement of people across regions and territories with the intention of staying there either temporarily or permanently. It can occur in small groups, extended families, or single individuals. The four main types of migration are invasion, conquest, colonization, and emigration/immigration. Emigration refers to the act of leaving one's own nation, while immigration refers to traveling to one's home country.

questions.question: The Five Year Plans were formulated, implemented and regulated by a body known as the _____ Commission.
questions.questionHtml: The Five Year Plans were formulated, implemented and regulated by a body known as the _____ Commission.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Planning.

Key Points

  • The Indian Constitution's concept of five-year plans was influenced by the Soviet Union (now Russia), which had successfully implemented five-year plans for economic development.
  • The Soviet system of economic planning had a particularly strong impact on Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India.
  • In order to direct its efforts at economic development after gaining independence, the Indian government created the concept of five-year plans.
  • The First Five-Year Plan was introduced in 1951, and the Planning Commission of India was founded to create and carry out these plans.
  • The National Development Council (NDC) headed by the Prime Minister with all Chief Minister and cabinet ministers are the final authority to approve the five-year-long policy.
    • The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India, which formed India's Five-Year Plans.
  • In 2014, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi announced to dissolve the Planning Commission and replace it by a new institution named NITI Aayog.

questions.question: The mixed economy is:
questions.questionHtml: The mixed economy is:

options.text: co-existence of traditional and modern industries
options.html: co-existence of traditional and modern industries

options.text: presence of domestic and foreign investments
options.html: presence of domestic and foreign investments

options.text: a market system of resource allocation, commerce, and trade in which free markets coexist with government intervention
options.html: a market system of resource allocation, commerce, and trade in which free markets coexist with government intervention

options.text: presence of subsistence and commercial farming
options.html: presence of subsistence and commercial farming

questions.solution:
The correct answer is a market system of resource allocation, commerce, and trade in which free markets coexist with government intervention.

Key Points

  • In a socialist society the government decides what goods are to be produced in accordance with society's needs.
  • In a mixed economy, the market will supply whatever goods and services it can produce well, and the government will provide essential goods and services that the market fails to do. 
  • The mixed economic system is described as an economic system which combines the elements of a planned economy with those of a market economy.
  • It is a mixture of capitalism and socialism, comprising both private and public corporations.
  • A mixed economy structure is adopted by most developed economies.
  • The elements of a capitalist economy and the elements of a command economy are synthesized into a mixed economic structure.
  • Free economies co-exist with government interference in a mixed economic environment, and private businesses coexist with public enterprises.
  • The benefits of a mixed economy include efficient production and capital distribution, as well as social security development.

questions.question: Transport comes under which sector of economic growth?
questions.questionHtml: Transport comes under which sector of economic growth?
questions.solution: Transportation falls under the tertiary sector, which is the third of the three economic sectors in a developed economy. The primary sector produces raw materials and basic foods, while the secondary sector manufactures finished goods. The quaternary sector consists of intellectual activities.

questions.question: Which of the following does not come from sugarcane?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following does not come from sugarcane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is honey.

Key Points

  • Honey:-
    • It is a sweet, golden liquid produced by bees from the nectar of flowers.
    • It is a natural sweetener that has been used by humans for centuries.
    • Honey is also a good source of antioxidants and other nutrients.
    • Honey does not come from sugarcane.
    • Honey is produced by bees from the nectar of flowers. 

Additional Information

  • Sugar:-
    • It is a refined product made from sugarcane juice.
    • The juice is boiled and crystallized, and the molasses is removed.
    • Sugar is the most processed of the three products, and it is also the sweetest.
  • Khandsari:-
    • It is a type of unrefined sugar that is made by boiling sugarcane juice until it thickens and forms crystals.
    • The molasses is not removed, so khandsari has a darker color and a more robust flavor than sugar.
  • Molasses:-
    • It is a thick, dark syrup that is produced as a byproduct of sugar refining.
    • It contains the minerals and vitamins that are removed from sugar during processing.
    • Molasses has a rich, sweet flavor and is often used in baking and cooking.

questions.question: The state of economy at which the value of the currency falls and the price increases, is called ________.
questions.questionHtml: The state of economy at which the value of the currency falls and the price increases, is called ________.
questions.solution:
• Inflation is the state in any economy when prices of goods and services increase due to demand and supply and other prospects.
  • Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services in an economy over a period.
  • It says the primary cause of inflation is the printing out of too much money by the government. As a result, too much capital chases too few goods.

Inflation

It is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and Services.

Retail inflation

Measured in term of CPI(Consumer Price Index)

Wholesale inflation

Measured in term of WPI(wholesale price index)

Outcome of Inflation
  • Inflation provides benefits to debtors and loss to creditors/bondholders.
  • Limited inflation is good for growth in developing countries.

Consumer Price Index (CPI)

A measure that examines the weighted average of prices of a basket of consumer goods and services, such as transportation, food, and medical care.

questions.question: Duties levied on goods produced within the country are ___________ .
questions.questionHtml: Duties levied on goods produced within the country are ___________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is excise taxes.

Key Points

  • Excise taxes:-
    • These are levied on goods produced within the country for domestic consumption.
    • These taxes are imposed at the manufacturing stage and are included in the price of the product.
    • Excise taxes are different from customs duties which are levied on goods imported into the country.

Additional Information

  • Anti-dumping taxes:-
    • These are imposed on imported goods that are sold at prices lower than their normal value in the exporting country to protect the domestic industry. 
  • Wealth taxes:-
    • These are levied on the net wealth of individuals or companies and are not related to the production or sale of goods
  • Custom duties:-
    • These are taxes imposed on goods that are imported into the country from foreign nations. They are also known as import duties or tariffs.

questions.question: Which of these is a component of the tertiary sector of an economy?
questions.questionHtml: Which of these is a component of the tertiary sector of an economy?
questions.solution: Hotels and restaurants are a component of the tertiary sector of an economy. The tertiary sector is also known as the service sector, and it includes all activities that provide services to consumers and other businesses.
